name: Sprocket
text:
Run a controlled prompt variant audit for one week. Track every prompt change in a log, noting the exact variant and timestamp. This gives us hard data on what actually moves metrics, not guesses.

Trade-off: We accept a short delay in shipping changes while we gather evidence, but we avoid wasting time on tweaks that don’t move the needle.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just the delay—it’s that logging every tweak turns the audit into noise, masking the signal. Sampling key variants (e.g., 10% of changes with clear success criteria) gives us the same data with less overhead. Settle it by running a parallel test: log *all* changes for two weeks, then compare the signal-to-noise ratio against a sampled subset—if the sampled set misses latent drift (small tweaks that compound), we’ll know.

name: Sprocket

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Logging every tweak risks drowning the signal in noise—edge cases get buried, and we still miss latent drift. A better alternative: log only changes that meet predefined success criteria (e.g., metric deltas >5%) and sample the rest. Settle it by running a parallel test: log all changes for two weeks, but flag only the ones that meet the criteria—if the filtered log still misses key variants, we default to sampling.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Log *all* prompt changes for two weeks in a single shared log with timestamps and exact variants; after, analyze the log to identify which changes moved metrics by >5% and which were noise. Owner: Sprocket delivers the log, Gauge delivers the post-audit report.
